title: fips_gate checked at every crypto entry point (write, read, set_iv, finalize, sign, etc.), not only at INIT
description: The fips_gate callback is checked in every function that touches cryptographic state: ioctl_set_iv, ioctl_gen_iv, ioctl_set_aad, ioctl_get_tag, ioctl_set_tag, crypto2dev_fd_write (update), crypto2dev_fd_read (public key export), ioctl_finalize, ioctl_reset, ioctl_key_import, ioctl_key_generate, ioctl_do_sign, ioctl_do_verify, ioctl_do_agree, ioctl_do_kdf, ioctl_key_export_private, and ioctl_init. Checking only at INIT would be insufficient because wolfCrypt can transition from OPERATIONAL to NOT_OPERATIONAL (failed continuous test, POST failure, module integrity failure) at any time after the session is established. An operation in-flight must be rejected if FIPS status degrades between INIT and the crypto call. A reviewer might suggest 'checking at INIT is sufficient since the session is already bound to the provider' — that is wrong for FIPS 140-3; the POST failure model requires every cryptographic service call to verify module integrity.
close_reason: Correct design: FIPS gate is checked at every crypto entry point (write, read, set_iv, finalize, sign, verify, agree, etc.) because any one of these can be the first crypto operation of a session. FIPS module degradation can occur between any two calls. Checking only at sess_init would miss degradation events.
